notes:
I couldn't do this research. My first attempt to read the sites failed with a message saying I had no tool calls left for this turn, and a second, simpler try failed the same way. That was the only tool that can reach the web, so I didn't open any of the pages, including Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Precept Austin, Wesley and the NET Bible notes.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say and give a URL for each point. Because nothing loaded, I have no notes to give you. I haven't written commentary from memory, since that would break your rule.

If you ask again in a new message, my tool access should reset, and I'll start with these:
- **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:** enduringword.com (Proverbs 16), studylight.org (Gill and Wesley's notes), biblehub.com (Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary), preceptaustin.org.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** v. 4 (God making "even the wicked" for disaster), v. 6 (iniquity "atoned for" by loving devotion), and vv. 1, 9 and 33 (God's control versus human plans). For each I'd look at the tradition's own teachers, for example Reformed (Ligonier, Monergism), Wesleyan (wesley.nnu.edu, Seedbed), Baptist (Desiring God, GTY) and Lutheran (LCMS, 1517).
- **Other views:** netbible.org notes, Catholic and Orthodox readings (newadvent.org, catholic.com, oca.org), and anything on prosperity readings of v. 3 or v. 20.

You could also ask for the chapter in parts, such as vv. 1–11, 12–22 and 23–33, which uses fewer tool calls each time.
